children: Markets deepened their losses through the mid-session on Wednesday, with the Sensex shedding 813.20 points, or 1.09 per cent, to 74,015.05 and the Nifty 50 falling 265 points, or 1.13 per cent, to 23,181.80 as of 1.18 pm, extending the sharp gap-down open that set the tone at the start of trade. The losses widened from the opening levels, when the Sensex had opened at 74,272.40 and the Nifty at 23,221.80, as selling pressure intensified across financial, metals and insurance counters.

Financial stocks continued to lead the decline. HDFC Life Insurance remained the worst performer on the Nifty 50, falling 5.05 per cent to ₹533.15 from a previous close of ₹561.50. Bajaj Finance was down 4.95 per cent to ₹991.60 from ₹1,043.20, while Axis Bank shed 4.67 per cent to ₹1,185.10 from ₹1,243.20. Bajaj Finserv declined 3.83 per cent to ₹1,775.70 from ₹1,846.50. Hindalco Industries joined the losers, dropping 2.29 per cent to ₹980.80 from ₹1,003.80, marking a broadening of the sell-off into the metals space.

On the options front, meaningful call writing was seen across the 23,300 and 23,400 strikes, while the 23,200 put had substantial open interest, followed by the 23,100 strike, reflecting the market’s defensive positioning. The Nifty’s Advance-Decline Ratio stood at a lopsided 7:43, underscoring the breadth of the selling. On the BSE, of 4,330 stocks traded, 2,630 advanced, 1,446 declined and 254 remained unchanged, with 159 stocks hitting 52-week highs and 62 at 52-week lows.
Only four Nifty stocks in positive territory

Only four Nifty 50 stocks were in positive territory through mid-session. Cipla led the gainers, rising 1.98 per cent to ₹1,410.40 from a previous close of ₹1,383.00, as the pharma sector showed resilience. SBI Life Insurance reversed its morning losses to trade 0.36 per cent higher at ₹1,766.40 from ₹1,760.00. Bharat Electronics gained 0.24 per cent to ₹397.00 from ₹396.05, and NTPC edged up a marginal 0.02 per cent to ₹326.05 from ₹326.00. Nifty Realty was the best performing sector, while Nifty Private Bank was the worst.
Crude, Treasury yields weigh on sentiment

The dual pressure of WTI crude near $91 per barrel and the US 10-year Treasury yield around 5.118 per cent, near its highest level since 2007, continued to define the session’s direction.banking and financial stocks are seeing more pronounced weakness in the opening trade, underperforming the broader market as investors turn more defensive.”

Technically, the Nifty’s immediate support lies at 23,040–23,060, with the next cushion at 22,870–22,890 if that zone gives way. Resistance is placed at 23,350–23,370, with a move above 23,370 potentially extending a rally toward 23,520. On the Sensex, support is seen at 73,700 and resistance at 74,500. The rupee was also under pressure, trading near ₹95.80–96.10 per dollar, with the USD/INR RSI at 59 and rising, reflecting building dollar strength.
Geopolitical concerns keep risk appetite in check

The geopolitical backdrop, centred on the unresolved US-Iran standoff and the scheduled Trump-Xi meeting, kept risk appetite in check, with traders likely to track crude prices and bond yields closely for any directional shift through the second half of the session.

title: Sensex slides 813 points, financial stocks tumble as crude oil and bond yields pressure markets
